title: Muyu people - Wikipedia
text: The Muyu speak Muyu languages, which traditionally are divided into multiple dialects according to Muyu sub-tribes. Linguists initially classified them as either North Muyu (Ninati) and South Muyu (Metomka), along with Yonggom and Ningrum languages.

title: Muyu language - Wikipedia
text: Language family. Trans–New Guinea.Muyu, Moyu,[2] is one of the Ok languages of South Papua, Indonesia. Based on available resources, linguists divided it to two varieties Kadi (North Muyu) and South Muyu.

title: Muyu language — Grokipedia
text: The Muyu language, a Lowland Ok member of the Trans-New Guinea phylum, predominantly follows a subject-object-verb (SOV) word order in its basic clauses, reflecting a verb-final typology common in Papuan languages.

text: South Muyu is an endangered indigenous language of Indonesia. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by a decreasing number of young people.
